title: RLUSD escrow today: AllowTrustLineLocking issuer permission and TEST-SGD
abstract: Why RLUSD cannot be escrowed today without issuer permission, and what AllowTrustLineLocking means for token escrow experiments.
tags: RLUSD escrow blockers and the TEST-SGD substitute
body:
RLUSD escrow support cannot be inferred from an XRP key-reveal purchase. The team documented official RLUSD as blocked until its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking. Our alternative is TEST-SGD, an IOU issued by our own Testnet issuer with no real value. It stands in for RLUSD in a mechanism experiment; it is neither official RLUSD nor evidence of stablecoin adoption. The docs contain no verified list of Singapore banks piloting RLUSD settlement in 2026. We cannot name banks from this evidence.

A dedicated issuer creates TEST-SGD tokens on Testnet for experiments; these tokens carry no economic value and substitute for RLUSD only in mechanism tests. S$ prices map 1:1 to TEST-SGD; this is neither a peg nor a backing claim.

The issuer is separate from buyer and writer. Policy rejects issuer-as-party, missing permission, nonzero transfer fees, frozen/unauthorized lines, insufficient balance or destination limit before create signing. This is a conservative subset of XLS-85: no transfer-fee arithmetic or freeze exception is claimed. Settlement checks the writer RippleState balance delta (currency, issuer, sign and exact value), never the requested Amount as proof of delivery. Cancellation checks the buyer's returned balance delta. The buyer retains its original budget reservation while an outcome is unresolved.

The issuer, buyer and writer are separate parties. The experimental issuer enables token locking before the buyer and writer establish eligible trust lines. A successful TEST-SGD escrow proves only that this configured stand-in worked on Testnet. It does not change the official RLUSD issuer's permissions or establish a live bank settlement partnership.
